questions.question: What is the core idea behind T5 (Text-To-Text Transfer Transformer)?
options: Convert all NLP tasks into a unified text-to-text format: input text in, output text out
Use a larger BERT model
Replace attention with convolutions
Train separate models per task
questions.explanation: T5 reformulates every NLP task as text-to-text. Translation becomes 'translate English to German: ...', summarization becomes 'summarize: ...', classification becomes predicting a label word. A single model and objective (cross-entropy on output tokens) handles all tasks.

questions.question: What is BART's pre-training objective?
options: Next-token prediction (causal LM)
Masked language modeling
Reconstruct original text from noised/corrupted inputs via encoder-decoder
Contrastive learning between sentence pairs
questions.explanation: BART uses denoising auto-encoding: corrupt the input (token masking, deletion, rotation, text infilling) and train the decoder to reconstruct the original sequence. This makes BART especially good at generation tasks like summarization and translation.

questions.question: When would you choose an encoder-decoder model (T5/BART) over a decoder-only model (GPT)?
options: For tasks with long context windows
For tasks requiring conditioning on a full input sequence (summarization, translation, Q&A) where bidirectional encoding of the source helps
For tasks requiring fast inference
For classification tasks
questions.explanation: Encoder-decoder models shine when you have a source sequence to fully encode before generating — summarization, translation, structured prediction. The encoder can attend bidirectionally to the source, which helps understanding. Decoder-only models are simpler and dominate open-ended generation.

questions.question: What span corruption objective does T5 use during pre-training?
options: Mask individual tokens like BERT's MLM
Mask contiguous spans of tokens and replace each span with a single sentinel token
Drop full sentences from the input
Shuffle the order of tokens
questions.explanation: T5 masks spans (not individual tokens) and replaces each masked span with a unique sentinel token (e.g., <extra_id_0>). The decoder must predict the masked spans in sequence. This is harder than token-level MLM and leads to better representations for generation.

questions.question: What key difference between T5 and BART affects their best use cases?
options: T5 is English-only; BART is multilingual
T5 was pre-trained with a text-to-text reconstruction objective emphasizing understanding; BART was pre-trained with stronger noise corruption better tuned for generation
T5 uses ReLU, BART uses GELU
T5 uses absolute positional encoding; BART uses RoPE
questions.explanation: T5's span-masking objective produces strong representations for understanding and generation. BART's heavier noise (text infilling, sentence shuffling) makes it especially strong at generation tasks. In practice BART tends to outperform on summarization; T5 on multi-task NLP benchmarks.
